product_from_film: Skillsync helps recruiters find engineers from open-source contributions using a natural-language search.
explains_well: Three domain searches connect specialist work to contribution cards and outreach messages.
unclear: The film jumps from a typed query to a person, without showing the search results or why that person ranked.
scenario: Find compiler, drone and quantum specialists from their contributions.
product_clear_basis: Search-result text describes finding engineers from open-source contributions; the Skillsync search follows.

categories.finding: Queries, contribution labels and messages convey recruiting without sound, but ranking logic is absent.
Large query crops lead to faces, then floating cards and messages; the face/card competition can limit reading.
Three domains fit into roughly 22s, prioritizing breadth over evidence for any one candidate.
The question of finding strong engineers is answered conceptually through contribution search, not a visible ranking decision.
Recognizable work environments and direct outreach suggest discovery and opportunity; response unmeasured.
The query/card/message pattern persists; no selected result links the search to each person.
Search relevance, elite status, real candidate identity and successful hiring are unverified. Messages illustrate outreach only.
Contribution-based specialist searches distinguish the offer more than generic recruiter imagery.
